quiz.why: A later request must first wait in the queue until the earlier requests finish. The waiting time counts toward TTFT, so TTFT grows. Once its turn comes, the decode speed is the same as when used alone, and the answer quality does not change.

problem: Someone says, "this card runs at 90 token/s". Add a minimal checkable note to that statement: which conditions and statistics must it state at the very least?
answer: State: the GPU, CPU, RAM and driver; the engine version (commit hash) and build flags; the model file and quantization (ideally with a hash); the actual number of input and output tokens; the KV cache, chunking and draft settings, and whether the caches were cold or warm; the number of requests active at the same time; the sampling parameters; the formula for "speed" and where timing starts and stops (for example N ÷ decode time); how many warm-up runs, how many timed repetitions and in what order; report the median and the min–max range, and list the first run on its own; attach every run's raw record, the number of failures and the quality-check results. Without these, it is just one observation that was never properly described.

title: Capstone project: build an explainable inference machine
deck: Open up one thin vertical slice first, then add features layer by layer. What you deliver is not just code that runs, but the reason for every trade-off and the evidence for every component.
prereq: Finish the learning track you chose; Chapters 26 (testing) and 27 (measurement) are required.
goals: Plan a course project "vertical slice first", so the first feature produces checkable real data as early as possible
Write up an engineering trade-off as "decision, gain, cost, verification, when to revisit"
Label each component with its evidence stage, and check your report against the rubric

quiz.text: Every part of Strata's PLE module passed its comparison test, yet the whole-model acceptance check failed. What is the most direct reason?
choices: The comparison tests' tolerance was set too loose
The model's main path never called these parts
The graphics card did not have enough VRAM
quiz.why: The source comment says it plainly: the parts were all built and passed their comparison tests, but the model code never called them. Part-level tests can only prove that a part itself is correct, not that it is wired into the system. Only a test that walks the whole main path can catch this.

quiz.text: A course project has 10 weeks and 4 features, and each feature goes through 4 steps: write the code, write the tests, wire it into the main path, and leave evidence. To have something to demo at the deadline, which approach is safer?
choices: Write all the features' code first, then write all the tests and do all the wiring together
Get one feature running completely from input to output, then do the next
Write the code for the hardest feature first
quiz.why: With vertical slices first, the first feature runs end to end by week 4, and two do by week 10; built horizontally, none does by week 10. Vertical slices also expose a wrong interface assumption when the first feature is wired in, so the rework is smallest.

quiz.text: One of your components is fully written and wired into the main path, but it has not yet produced a complete record from real input. What should the report say?
choices: Write "done"
Write "wired into the main path, no real data yet"
Leave this component out for now
quiz.why: Label evidence honestly by stage: code written, on the main path, real data, or simulated. "Done" makes readers think it has already produced real results; leaving it out hides your progress. Only by stating exactly which step it stopped at can readers judge.

problem: Write an optimization hypothesis that you are willing to have an experiment refute, and say which result would make you give it up.
answer: Example: keeping the model file, the input, the quality gate and the draft policy fixed, raising the budget for hot experts in VRAM should cut the time the CPU spends computing experts and raise end-to-end decode speed. Run the experiment with Chapter 27's method: after warm-up, repeat with A/B alternation and report the median and the range. If the hit rate rises but the extra swap-in overhead or resource contention leaves end-to-end speed no better, or the quality gate fails, give up this configuration and analyze which factor the model left out.
